subject: Initial-chunk delivery and streaming throughput for pilot
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia@aureliahealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Initial-chunk delivery and streaming throughput for pilot

Ben / Lauren —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. As we scope the pilot (speech-to-text transcripts fed into a streaming summarization pipeline), our infra and compliance teams are asking for explicit commitments on two items so we can sign off on test provisioning:

1) Initial-chunk delivery (we measure as time-to-first-chunk / first 32-token batch delivered to client) — what percentile and measurement window do you commit to for the hosted endpoint, and are exceptions available for pre-warmed or dedicated capacity?

2) Sustained emission rate (tokens/sec expectation) — we need guidance on steady-state throughput guarantees vs burst allowances and fallback behavior if the rate drops.

A couple of constraints: our incoming audio streams are long (45–90 minutes), average prompt prefix sizes are ~2–3k tokens, and latency sensitivity is for first-chunk under 500ms where possible. We understand hosted endpoints may be best-effort; we want clarity on where you can offer carve-outs or contractual exceptions for a dedicated pilot.

Attached: pilot-tech-brief.pdf (protocol, example transcripts). Can someone summarize a proposed SLA matrix and where exceptions are reasonable? We want to move to mutual action plan this week.

— Lydia
Director of Platform Engineering
Aurelia Health
Attachment: pilot-tech-brief.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lydia@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial-chunk delivery and streaming throughput for pilot

Lydia —

Really appreciate the clear constraints. Short answer: we can propose a two-track commitment (hosted best-effort vs dedicated pre-warmed). I'll loop Priyom (SE) and Lauren (AE) to draft a succinct SLA matrix and an exception path for pilot use.

Next steps from our side:
- Priyom: draft the technical carving options and measurement methods (p99 time-to-first-chunk over 1h windows at representative prompt lengths).
- We will propose a short mutual action plan and a short-term commitment for the dedicated pilot to ensure predictable behavior.

I'll follow up with a consolidated proposal by tomorrow EOD and include a simple two-row SLA matrix so your procurement can react quickly.

Thanks,
Ben
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: proposed exception language / measurements for Lydia

Team —

Quick internal note after Lydia's ask. Key trade-offs and suggested measurable definition so procurement can sign:

Proposal sketch (for the SLA doc):
- Tier A (Dedicated, pre-warmed): commit p95 time-to-first-chunk <= 120ms for prompt prefixes up to 3k tokens; sustained emission 250 tokens/sec (sustained = 5 minute rolling window), 95th percentile.
- Tier B (Hosted, best-effort): p95 time-to-first-chunk <= 400ms for prefixes up to 3k tokens; burst up to 500 tokens/sec for short bursts (60s) with graceful fallback to a smaller model or degraded tokens/sec with prior notice.

Exception request wording (for procurement/legal):
"Redwood may provide a pilot exception that temporarily specifies Tier A commitments for a defined fleet (dedicated pool) scheduled and warmed for the pilot window. This exception is limited to the pilot period and will be measured against the definitions above; production will be re-evaluated for scale."

Measurement notes to capture for Lydia's team:
- Measurement point: time-to-first-chunk measured at either the client-facing API ingress (preferred) or via server-side telemetry aggregated at edge.
- Percentile window: report p50/p95/p99 over 1h and 24h windows.
- Fallback behavior: automatic model routing and circuit breaker firing when sustained CPU/GPU utilization thresholds are exceeded.

Questions for Priyom: does the p95 120ms target look achievable for warmed pools with current kernel selection and our KV-cache strategies? If not, propose realistic numbers and any prep action (prefetching, prefix cache warm-up, or pre-compiling kernels).

Ben

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: proposed exception language / measurements for Lydia

Ben / Lauren —

Quick engineering take and a conservative set of numbers we can justify:

1) Feasibility: For pre-warmed dedicated pools on A100/H100-class GPUs with our current runtime and prefix caching, p95 time-to-first-chunk at ~150ms is realistic for 2–3k token prefixes if we prefetch KV and keep model kernels resident. Hitting 120ms tight but possible with some additional warm-up (scheduled dummy requests) immediately before the stream starts.

2) Hosted constraints: for shared pools, we recommend wording "best-effort" with expected p95 in 250–450ms depending on region and concurrent load. We should avoid hard contractual latency SLAs on shared multi-tenant pools.

3) Token throughput: we can guarantee sustained 200–300 tokens/sec in a dedicated pool (95th percentile over 5m windows). Bursts up to 600 tokens/sec for short durations (<= 90s) are possible but should not be in a live SLA unless dedicated bursting capacity is reserved.

4) Measurement method and telemetry: we will provide a CSV export: timestamp, model_variant, region, tokens_emitted, first_chunk_ms, 1h_p95_first_chunk, sustained_tokens_per_sec_5m. Recommend p95 over 1h for pilot reporting.

Draft exception paragraph for the SLA doc (suggested):
"Pilot Exception: During the pilot window (start/end dates), Redwood will allocate a dedicated pre-warmed pool for the customer to achieve the Tier A commitments above. Measurements will be collected and shared daily. This exception will automatically revert at the end of the pilot unless both parties agree to an expanded dedicated commitment."

I'll attach a short note on kernel selection and recommended warm-up steps.

— Priyom
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Lydia —

Thanks again for the context and the tech brief. Based on our internal review we've put together a short proposal and an explicit pilot exception that should address procurement and infra concerns. High-level summary below; attached is a one-page SLA matrix and an MAP for the pilot.

SLA summary (pilot exception):
- Tier A — Dedicated pre-warmed pool (pilot): p95 time-to-first-chunk <= 150ms for prompt prefixes up to 3k tokens; sustained emission: 200–300 tokens/sec (95th percentile over 5 minute windows). We will perform scheduled warm-up prior to each test window.
- Tier B — Hosted (general availability): best-effort p95 time-to-first-chunk 250–450ms depending on region and load; burst allowances up to 600 tokens/sec for short durations are best-effort unless reserved.

Measurement & reporting:
- We will provide daily CSV exports showing p50/p95/p99 time-to-first-chunk and sustained tokens/sec (5m windows). Measurement point: client-facing ingress; we can also share server-side metrics if you need correlation.

Fallback behavior:
- If sustained throughput constraints are hit, requests will automatically route to a pre-agreed smaller model and the client will receive degraded token/sec until capacity is restored. Circuit-breaker events will be logged and communicated within the MAP.

Attachments: SLA-proposal-redwood-v1.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MAP).

Next steps:
1) Can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to lock down pilot dates and acceptance criteria?
2) If procurement is comfortable with the exception wording below, we can generate a short addendum to the trial order.

Suggested addendum sentence:
"Redwood will provide the Tier A commitments for the pilot window as a temporary exception; production commitments will be re-evaluated and may require dedicated reserved capacity and/or additional pricing. The exception will be scoped by start/end dates and expected traffic profiles."

Would love to get your feedback and confirm a time for the sync.

Best,
Ben Carter
